title.title: No percolation at criticality on every quasi-transitive graph
title.subtitle: Claim: at $p_c$ there is no infinite cluster, on $\mathbb Z^3$ and on every quasi-transitive graph with $p_c < 1$

beats.text: Keep each edge with probability $p$: below $p_c$ clusters are finite, above, one is infinite
The question that defines the field: what happens exactly at $p_c$?
The finite tool is a relay inequality: reach $A$, then go on from the worst point of $A$

plain: Open each pipe in a huge grid by a coin flip: right at the tipping point, can water flow forever?

steps: Suppose an infinite cluster exists exactly at the threshold
Finitely many crossing estimates then survive slightly below it
Relay gluing builds an infinite cluster below threshold: impossible

voice.text: Keep each edge with probability p. Exactly at the threshold, can an infinite cluster exist?
If it could, it would also exist slightly below the threshold, which is impossible.
Claimed: never, on every such graph.
